data.did_you_know: In 1943, Time magazine declared Paul Robeson “probably the most famous living Negro” but his political activism led to him being blacklisted by 1950.
data.description: The actor, singer, and activist is seen here campaigning for Henry Wallace, presidential candidate for the Progressive Party, whose liberal views caused it to be associated with communism. Orkin was one of many photojournalists shooting up at the speaker. Instead of focusing just on Robeson, however, she widens the shot to include the curious sight of an array of photographers waiting to shoot the audience as they when they respond to Robeson’s powerful oratory.
data.creditline: Gift of Mary Engel/Ruth Orkin Photo Archive
